title: Query String
body:
The part of a [[URL]] after the `?`, made of `key=value` pairs joined by `&`:

`/products/search?query=shoes&page=2&limit=20`

It's how a GET request carries parameters, since GET has no body. The whole thing is sent to and read by the **server**, which parses it into a usable structure (`req.query` in [[Express]]). Values must be percent-encoded, since spaces and `&` would otherwise break the parse.

Typical uses are filtering, sorting, and [[Pagination]]. The important caution: a query string is fully visible — in the address bar, in browser history, in server logs, and in `Referer` headers sent to third parties — so credentials and tokens must never be put in one. Contrast with the `#fragment`, which never leaves your machine at all.
